title: Operator resilience fabric and offline fallback reference
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This reference describes the Operator Resilience Fabric (ORF): a lightweight control-plane and runtime pattern designed to keep customer-facing private deployments (VPC and on-prem) available when upstream control-plane connectivity is degraded or unavailable. The doc covers the architecture, failure modes, operator procedures for offline fallback, packaging and artifact requirements, day-2 operational checks, upgrade/rollback implications, and minimal customer readiness requirements.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Maintain tenant-serving availability (read/write inference requests) for defined SLO windows when the Redwood control plane or regional telemetry gateways are unreachable.
  - Provide deterministic fallback policies for model variants, KV cache warming, and admission control that preserve safety and cost bounds.
  - Ensure operator-run recoverability: clear escape hatches, rollforward and roll back steps, and forensic evidence preservation.
- Non-goals:
  - Full feature parity with hosted operational tooling while offline.
  - Arbitrary long-term autonomous operation without eventual reconciliation.

High-level architecture:
- Components (logical):
  - Local operator agent (operatord): lightweight process responsible for orchestration of fallback workflows, local policy enforcement, and artifact validation.
  - Runtime fabric (runtime-fabric): set of sidecar/daemon processes that manage model artifacts, KV cache, and inference runtime lifecycle on each node.
  - Local control-plane replica (lcpr): minimal control-plane cache containing routing policies, model manifests, and safety gates; canonical only while online, fallbacks use cached manifests with attestation.
  - Telemetry gateway (tg): local aggregator for sampling and buffering telemetry until upstream recovered.
- Data flows and invariants:
  - On connectivity loss: operatord consults lcpr and runtime-fabric to switch to fallback model variants and admission policies.
  - Safety invariant: no automatic escalation to higher-cost model variants beyond configured budget percentages without operator approval.

Topology patterns and reference diagrams (text):
- Local single-region resilient topology:
  - control-plane egress -> (proxy) -> operatord -> runtime-fabric -> GPU pool -> inference pods
  - When upstream broken, operatord sets runtime-fabric to local-only routing and engages read-through KV cache.
- Multi-AZ airgapped topology:
  - Each AZ runs an lcpr instance with quorum-based checks. operatord uses cross-AZ heartbeats to decide forced evacuation or model eviction.

SLOs and thresholds (recommended):
- Tenant-serving availability during upstream blackout: 99.5% over a 1-hour window for requests below max_seq_len 1024.
- Token latency increase cap: no more than 2x median baseline for degraded model variants; prefer queue-based admission to stay under 500ms p50 for short requests.
- Cost guardrail: local fallback must not increase per-token spend by > 40% for the first 30 minutes without explicit operator approval.

Operator playbook: offline fallback activation
1) Detection and initial validation:
   - Alert triggers: control-plane-e2e-heartbeat absent for > 45s or telemetry gateway unresponsive > 60s.
   - Validation steps:
     a) Confirm network disruption: curl -sSf https://control-plane.example.internal/health || true
     b) Check operator agent status: kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=operatord -o wide
2) Safe-mode entry (automated by operatord):
   - operatord writes a stamped event to lcpr and switches to 'fallback-pending' state.
   - Runtime-fabric changes (atomic): pause automated model refresh, freeze KV eviction for 60s, enable admission queue with configured thresholds.
3) Fallback candidate selection (automated with operator oversight):
   - Selection rules (in priority): local quantized variants with known throughput profiles; cached model v<X>.fallback; small-context variants for long-requests.
   - Example selection command (operator CLI):
     redwood-operatorctl select-fallback --tenant tenant-abc --budget 30
4) Operator validation and approval:
   - Operator inspects live metrics: redwood-operatorctl metrics --tenant tenant-abc --window 5m
   - Approve fallback: redwood-operatorctl approve-fallback --tenant tenant-abc --fallback-id fdl-20270114-01
5) Ramp and monitoring:
   - Ramp policy: 10% traffic -> 50% in 5m -> 100% in 15m if SLOs hold.
   - Continuous checks: token latency p50/p95, KV hit rate, local disk utilization > 80% triggers eviction policies.
6) Recovery and reconciliation:
   - When upstream control plane reachable, operatord enters reconciliation: replay buffered telemetry, validate model manifests (checksum+signature), and gradually re-enable centralized routing.
   - Evidence bundle exported: operatord bundle-evidence --since 2027-01-14T08:00Z --out /tmp/evidence.tar.gz

Day-2 checks and runbook snippets:
- Daily automated check list (cron):
  - lcpr sync age < 5m when online.
  - KV cache hit rate > 75% under baseline workloads.
  - operatord health probes all green.
- One-click operator commands:
  - Verify fallback readiness: redwood-operatorctl readiness-check --tenant tenant-abc
  - Force local-only mode (escape hatch): redwood-operatorctl set-mode --tenant tenant-abc --mode local-only --reason "egress-failure"

Packaging and artifact requirements:
- Immutable artifact bundles required for offline operation (sha256 + signature). Each bundle must include:
  - model weights (quantized variants), manifest.json, runtime shims, precompiled kernel list, and signature.asc
- Minimal version constraints:
  - operatord >= 1.8.0, runtime-fabric >= 3.2.1, lcpr schema v2 and manifest signing v1
- Example manifest snippet (JSON, shown as YAML for readability):
  manifest:
    models:
      - id: redwood-open-7b-q4f
        variant: q4f
        checksum: sha256:abcd1234...
        signed: true
      - id: redwood-open-70b-8bit
        variant: 8bit
        checksum: sha256:efgh5678...
        signed: true

Upgrade and rollback implications:
- Upgrade strategy while online:
  1) Staged rollout: canary to 1 node -> 5 nodes -> full. For ORF-critical components prefer operator-handshake stage where operatord hands off control to new agent and verifies signature chains.
  2) Artifact compatibility: new runtime-fabric versions must accept legacy manifest v1 for at least 48 hours.
- Offline upgrade constraints:
  - No upstream-driven upgrades should be applied during offline fallback. Operator-driven offline upgrade only after artifact attestation and operator approval.
- Rollback cookbook (stateful):
  - If a runtime upgrade causes KV inconsistency, steps:
    1) Quiesce inference routes (graceful drain existing requests).
    2) Snapshot current KV store: operatord kv snapshot --out /var/backups/kv-20270114.db
    3) Re-deploy previous runtime-fabric version from signed artifact store.
    4) Reconcile model manifests and rehydrate caches using snapshot replay.

Customer readiness and contractual minimums:
- Network:
  - Egress to Redwood control plane must be allowed initially for onboarding and periodic attestation.
  - MTU and BGP requirements: match documented carrier profiles; WAN RTT to nearest Redwood region < 120ms recommended for smooth reconciliation.
- Hardware and storage:
  - Local SSD for KV cache and artifact staging: minimum 1TB NVMe per GPU node with 150MB/s sustained write.
  - GPU compatibility: see our hardware-compatibility matrix; fallback requires models with quantized variants compatible with deployed accelerators.
- Security and evidence:
  - Customer must allow signature verification via customer KMS or provide public verification keys.
  - Proof-of-possession logs must be retained for 30 days for regulated deployments.

Operational metrics and dashboards (recommended panels):
- ORF Health: operatord-up, lcpr-sync-age, fallback-mode-active
- Performance: p50/p95 token latency, KV hit rate, model swap success rate
- Safety and cost: fallback-cost-multiplier, fallback-operator-approvals

Escalation and ownership:
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments (oncall rotation).
- Secondary: eng-sre (for incident bridging) and security (if evidence bundle flagged).
- Escalation ladder:
  1) oncall-private-deploy (pager)
  2) eng-private-deployments lead (paged)
  3) eng-sre mitigation lead

Appendix A — Example operatord config (YAML):

apiVersion: v1
kind: OperatorConfig
metadata:
  tenant: tenant-abc
settings:
  fallback_budget_percent: 30
  fallback_ramp: 
    initial_pct: 10
    steady_pct: 50
    full_pct: 100
  kv_cache_path: /var/lib/redwood/kv
  artifact_store: file:///opt/redwood/artifacts
  attest_timeout_seconds: 900
  metrics_export_interval_seconds: 15

Appendix B — Forensic evidence checklist:
- Signed manifest snapshots with timestamps
- Buffer telemetry bundle (min log retention 14 days locally)
- operatord events.log (structured) and system-level syslog
- checksums and signatures for artifacts used during fallback
